en: When looking at large language models, at AI
agents, you'll often hear the term tools.
And the idea behind tools is really just
that
you have a piece of software, an AI agent,
something like Claude Cowork or Claude Code,
for example, or something like the ChatGPT
app, no matter if it's running on your
system or on some other system, or maybe
also a piece of software you built yourself,
which tells a large language model that
you have a certain task for it, which is
your prompt, but that there also are certain
tools it may use. And which tools, that
simply depends on the software that
communicates with the large language model.
So with the ChatGPT app, for example, if
that software has a built-in tool or a
built-in code to read files, it can expose
that read file tool to the large language
model.
If it has a web search tool, it can expose
that.
But then the large language model doesn't
use the tool. Instead, it requests the tool
call. And then it's the surrounding
software, that ChatGPT app or whatever, that
does the actual tool call, that does
actually read the file, and that does then
send the result of that tool call, so the
content of a file, for example, back to the
model so that the model can keep on acting
and can keep on making decisions. But that's
really important. That is what the term tool
in the context of AI agents means it's
capabilities exposed by
the AI agent software, by the ChatGPT
software, for example, to the large language
model.
